samples.summary: `moveCells` freeze check scans the whole merge map, so one pre-existing straddling block refuses every row/column reorder on the sheet
samples.evidence: `const movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst); for (const [anchorSref, span] of movedMerges) { if (this.crossesFreezePane(...)) { this.refuse('merge-move-frozen'); return false; } }` iterates the *entire* post-move merge map, not just the blocks the move actually relocates. `moveMergeMap` maps an unaffected merge to itself, so a block that already straddles the boundary — which the code itself admits is reachable (merge.test.ts:835 seeds exactly that state via the store, and any document saved before this change could hold it, since `setFreezePane` did not snap) — makes the condition true for *any* src/dst. Every drag-reorder of unrelated rows then silently writes nothing and shows "Can't move a merged cell across a frozen row or column". Contrast `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2850), which correctly checks only `movedMerges` (blocks inside the source range). The check should be restricted to merges whose mapped position actually changed.

samples.summary: Backend move guard has the same over-broad scan: a pre-existing straddling merge 409s every `POST move` on the tab
samples.evidence: `const moved = moveMergeMap(merges, axis, srcIndex, count, dstIndex); for (const [anchorSref, span] of moved) { if (crossesFreezePane(range, frozenRows, frozenCols)) throw new ConflictException(...) }` loops the full moved map. A merge that already straddles the freeze (written by an older client, an XLSX import, or `POST insert`/`delete`, which do not snap — see worksheet-structure.controller.ts:347) is mapped to itself and trips the check for every move request, so the endpoint becomes permanently unusable for that tab even for moves nowhere near the merge or the boundary.

samples.summary: `POST insert`/`delete` still creates the straddling-merge state the new guards exist to prevent — the backend shift does not snap the freeze the way `Sheet.shiftCells` now does
samples.evidence: `applyShift` calls `applyWorksheetShift` only. `shiftWorksheetViewState` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:246-265) mirrors the *old* `Sheet.shiftCells` freeze adjustment but has no `snapFreezePastMerges` pass, while `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1415-1429) now snaps after shifting merges. So an API insert/delete that moves the boundary and the merge map independently can leave a block across the freeze — the exact 'one door into a state the editor cannot paint' the new `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` doc claims to close — and, combined with the previous finding, then 409s every subsequent move.

samples.summary: Freeze snapping is unbounded: a wide/tall merged block silently freezes far more of the sheet than the user asked for, including on unrelated inserts
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` sets `rows = range[1].r` / `cols = range[1].c`, i.e. the far edge of the offending block, with no cap. A merged banner `A1:Z1` (very common) plus "freeze first column" yields `frozenCols = 26` — the whole viewport width becomes the frozen pane. A full-column merge (`mergeSelection` over column A is permitted when no freeze exists) plus `setFreezePane(1,0)` yields `frozenRows = 1000000`, and `buildFreezeState` (view/layout.ts:149) computes `frozenHeight = rowDim.getOffset(frozenRows + 1)`, so the scrolling body is pushed entirely off screen. Worse, sheet.ts:1418 now applies the same snap on *every* `shiftCells`, so an unrelated row insert can silently jump the freeze line in a legacy document that already holds a straddling block. `setFreezePane` returns void, so nothing tells the caller the stored boundary differs from the requested one (the backend at least reports it).

samples.summary: `revalidateCopyBuffer` silently does nothing when the copied range lies past axis-ID coverage, leaving the stale index-keyed paste it exists to prevent
samples.evidence: `if (!buffer?.sourceAnchors) return;` — and `anchorsForRange` returns undefined whenever `refToAnchor` cannot resolve either corner (a copy of rows beyond `store.getRowOrder()` length, which is ordinary for a sparse sheet). In that case a remote insert/delete/reorder renumbers the snapshotted cells and the buffer survives, so a later internal paste relocates formulas and now re-creates merged blocks from stale coordinates — the failure mode the method was added for. A safer default would be to drop the buffer when anchors cannot be recorded.
searchedFor: grep reloadDimensions callers in frontend + sheets

samples.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` is O(n^2) in merge count on a server request path with no bound on the number of merges
samples.evidence: The `while (changed)` loop rescans every merge entry after any growth. `parseMerges` bounds cells *per* merge (MaxMergedCells) but never the *number* of merges, so a document with a long chain of merges each just past the previous one makes `PUT .../freeze` do O(n^2) `parseRef` calls inside `doc.update`, blocking the request. A single pass over merges sorted by start index would be linear.

samples.summary: `PUT freeze` now parses every stored merge key, so a malformed key 500s an endpoint that previously did not touch merges
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges(safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges ?? {}), rows, cols)` calls `parseRef` on each stored key; `parseRef` throws a bare `Error('Invalid Reference')` (coordinates.ts:351), which Nest turns into a 500 rather than a typed error. Any document whose merge map contains a key the engine did not write (peer client, importer) now makes the freeze endpoint fail instead of storing the boundary.

samples.summary: A pending cut now survives an intervening external paste, so the delete-at-source can fire much later than the gesture
samples.evidence: The view no longer calls `clearCopyBuffer()` after `paste`, and `Sheet.paste` only drops the buffer on the branch where `text === copyBuffer.text`. After a cut, a paste of unrelated clipboard text takes the external branch and leaves `isCut: true` in the buffer; a later paste whose text happens to match re-arms the cut and deletes the source cells. Previously the unconditional clear closed this.

finding.summary: `moveCells` freeze check scans the whole merge map, so one pre-existing straddling block refuses every row/column reorder on the sheet
finding.evidence: `const movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst); for (const [anchorSref, span] of movedMerges) { if (this.crossesFreezePane(...)) { this.refuse('merge-move-frozen'); return false; } }` iterates the *entire* post-move merge map, not just the blocks the move actually relocates. `moveMergeMap` maps an unaffected merge to itself, so a block that already straddles the boundary — which the code itself admits is reachable (merge.test.ts:835 seeds exactly that state via the store, and any document saved before this change could hold it, since `setFreezePane` did not snap) — makes the condition true for *any* src/dst. Every drag-reorder of unrelated rows then silently writes nothing and shows "Can't move a merged cell across a frozen row or column". Contrast `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2850), which correctly checks only `movedMerges` (blocks inside the source range). The check should be restricted to merges whose mapped position actually changed.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. sheet.ts:1552-1558 iterates the entire post-move merge map returned by moveMergeMap and refuses on any straddling block, not just relocated ones; merging.ts:161-176 + remapIndex (merging.ts:110-136) map unaffected merges to themselves, so a pre-existing straddling block makes the condition true for every src/dst. That state is reachable: setFreezePane snaps (sheet.ts:532-537) but loadFreezePane (sheet.ts:556-560) and loadMerges (sheet.ts:577-579) assign store values verbatim without snapping, and the repo's own test merge.test.ts:833-858 seeds and asserts exactly that state, documenting that a peer or the v1 settings API can write it into the document. Only shiftCells (sheet.ts:1417-1428) repairs it, and only on insert/delete, so a document that is opened and then reordered never repairs. Result: moveCells returns false before store.moveCells (sheet.ts:1564), so every row/column reorder silently no-ops with a 'merge-move-frozen' message (view/worksheet.ts:114) — and crossesFreezePane (merging.ts:189-193) tests both axes, so even an unrelated-axis move is blocked. The contrast case is also accurate: moveRangeTo (sheet.ts:2832, 2850-2860) checks only blocks inside the source range. No earlier guard prevents it; the only prior check is isMergeSplitByMove (sheet.ts:1540-1545), which an untouched merge passes. Correctness lane (wrong condition / broken core flow), major impact.

finding.summary: Backend move guard has the same over-broad scan: a pre-existing straddling merge 409s every `POST move` on the tab
finding.evidence: `const moved = moveMergeMap(merges, axis, srcIndex, count, dstIndex); for (const [anchorSref, span] of moved) { if (crossesFreezePane(range, frozenRows, frozenCols)) throw new ConflictException(...) }` loops the full moved map. A merge that already straddles the freeze (written by an older client, an XLSX import, or `POST insert`/`delete`, which do not snap — see worksheet-structure.controller.ts:347) is mapped to itself and trips the check for every move request, so the endpoint becomes permanently unusable for that tab even for moves nowhere near the merge or the boundary.

verdict.reason: The described code exists verbatim: assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:173-196) maps the whole merge record through moveMergeMap and throws ConflictException for ANY resulting range that crossesFreezePane. moveMergeMap/moveMerge (merging.ts:161-176, 103-137) copy every merge through remapIndex, so merges untouched by the move are mapped to themselves and still scanned — meaning one pre-existing straddling merge makes every POST /move on that tab 409, including moves far from the merge or the boundary, and including moves that would remove the straddle. I could not find a guard that makes the straddling state unreachable: worksheet-shape-migration.ts:444-450 copies legacy merges plus frozenRows/frozenCols verbatim with no snap, seed-templates.ts:140 assigns frozenRows directly without snapFreezePastMerges, and the documents are Yorkie CRDTs where a concurrent merge-cells and set-freeze from two clients are both accepted with no server-side revalidation (snapFreezePastMerges is only called at worksheet.controller.ts:112 and sheet.ts:533/1418). One supporting claim of the finding is inaccurate — POST insert/delete does appear to preserve the invariant, since shiftWorksheetViewState (worksheet-structure.ts:246-265) moves the freeze in lockstep with shiftMergeAxis (merging.ts:31-60) — but that only removes one provenance path, not the defect, so no named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: `POST insert`/`delete` still creates the straddling-merge state the new guards exist to prevent — the backend shift does not snap the freeze the way `Sheet.shiftCells` now does
finding.evidence: `applyShift` calls `applyWorksheetShift` only. `shiftWorksheetViewState` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:246-265) mirrors the *old* `Sheet.shiftCells` freeze adjustment but has no `snapFreezePastMerges` pass, while `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1415-1429) now snaps after shifting merges. So an API insert/delete that moves the boundary and the merge map independently can leave a block across the freeze — the exact 'one door into a state the editor cannot paint' the new `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` doc claims to close — and, combined with the previous finding, then 409s every subsequent move.

verdict.reason: The snap call is literally absent from the backend shift path, but the defect it is said to enable cannot occur. `applyWorksheetShift` uses the same `shiftMergeMap` and a character-for-character identical freeze adjustment as `Sheet.shiftCells` (worksheet-structure.ts:249-265 vs sheet.ts:1390-1413; worksheet-structure.ts:575-583 vs sheet.ts:1370), and that pairing preserves the no-straddle invariant for every insert/delete from a valid state: for a merge inside the band, E' = E - d_E and F' = F - d_F with d_F >= d_E and (d_F - d_E) <= F - E so E' <= F'; for a merge below the band, a delete that overlaps it forces delEnd >= S > F, so F' = i-1 is strictly less than the new anchor i. The repo's own tests say the same thing: merge.test.ts:825-830 documents an insert inside the frozen band with a merged block and concludes "no snapping needed", while the only tests where the snap fires (merge.test.ts:833-858, 860-874) must deliberately seed a store with an already-straddling merge, explicitly described as "a state this replica cannot create". The snap in shiftCells therefore repairs pre-existing corruption arriving from a peer; it is not what keeps shift from creating a straddle. Every v1 write path that could create one is already guarded: PUT freeze snaps (worksheet.controller.ts:112-119), PUT merges 409s on a crossing block (worksheet.controller.ts:184-200), and the move endpoint 409s (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:173-196). The only residual behavior is failing to repair an already-corrupt document, which the next editor shiftCells self-heals — defensive, not the major insert/delete-creates-it bug claimed.

finding.summary: Freeze snapping is unbounded: a wide/tall merged block silently freezes far more of the sheet than the user asked for, including on unrelated inserts
finding.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` sets `rows = range[1].r` / `cols = range[1].c`, i.e. the far edge of the offending block, with no cap. A merged banner `A1:Z1` (very common) plus "freeze first column" yields `frozenCols = 26` — the whole viewport width becomes the frozen pane. A full-column merge (`mergeSelection` over column A is permitted when no freeze exists) plus `setFreezePane(1,0)` yields `frozenRows = 1000000`, and `buildFreezeState` (view/layout.ts:149) computes `frozenHeight = rowDim.getOffset(frozenRows + 1)`, so the scrolling body is pushed entirely off screen. Worse, sheet.ts:1418 now applies the same snap on *every* `shiftCells`, so an unrelated row insert can silently jump the freeze line in a legacy document that already holds a straddling block. `setFreezePane` returns void, so nothing tells the caller the stored boundary differs from the requested one (the backend at least reports it).

verdict.reason: The code is present as described: snapFreezePastMerges (merging.ts:213-230) grows frozen counts to `range[1].r` / `range[1].c` with no upper bound, and Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:532-537) stores the snapped value and returns void, so a caller asking to freeze 1 column can silently end up with 26 frozen columns from a common A1:Z1 banner merge. sheet.ts:1418-1429 applies the same snap on every shiftCells and persists the changed boundary, so an insert/delete unrelated to the block can move the freeze line in a document holding a pre-existing straddling merge (an explicitly acknowledged state, docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:126-129). No guard bounds the result downstream: buildFreezeState (view/layout.ts:148-149) derives frozenWidth/frozenHeight straight from getOffset(frozen+1) with no viewport clamp, and the renderer loops the frozen quadrants over the full frozen extent (gridcanvas.ts:329-332, 400-405), so the scrolling body can be pushed off screen and per-frame work scales with the snapped count. One sub-claim in the evidence is wrong — a full-column merge is not reachable via mergeSelection, since canMergeSelection rejects non-'cell' selections (sheet.ts:4843) and header selection sets selectionType='column' (sheet.ts:3620) — but the reachable banner case alone makes the finding real, so it does not refute. I found no cap, no clamp, and no caller-side check anywhere, and the snap is reachable on a normal-use path (freeze a column on a sheet with a merged header row), which is wrong behavior a user will actually meet.

finding.summary: `undo`/`redo` renumber cells (structural undo) but do not clear the copy buffer, bypassing the new `shiftCells`/`moveCells` invalidation invariant
finding.evidence: The new doc on `clearCopyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2217-2222) states "every edit that renumbers the cells it snapshotted (`shiftCells`, `moveCells`) must call this", and the diff adds the call in both. But `undo()` (sheet.ts:5306) and `redo()` (sheet.ts:5338) re-load merges/dimensions/freeze from the store and can undo an insert/delete of rows or a row reorder — which renumbers exactly those cells — without calling `clearCopyBuffer()`. Sequence: insert rows → copy A1:B1 (merged) → Ctrl+Z (row insert undone, everything shifts) → Ctrl+V: `paste` still matches the clipboard text, relocates the grid from the stale `sourceRange`, and now also re-creates merged blocks at stale coordinates (`planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges`). Before this change the view cleared the buffer after every paste, so the window in which a stale buffer could be used was much smaller. The same gap exists for remote collaborators' structural edits, which never go through this Sheet's `shiftCells`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `undo()`/`redo()` renumber cells without clearing the copy buffer. Both do clear it: `undo()` calls `this.clearCopyBuffer()` at sheet.ts:5365 (with a comment stating an undone step may be a row/column insert, delete or reorder and the buffer goes either way to stop a later paste relocating and re-creating merged blocks from stale coordinates), and `redo()` calls it at sheet.ts:5399. The doc comment the finding quotes (sheet.ts:2217-2224) itself enumerates `shiftCells`, `moveCells`, `sortFilterByColumn`, and `undo`/`redo` — not just the two the finding says. The secondary claim about remote collaborators is likewise covered: peer edits arrive as a reload and are handled by `revalidateCopyBuffer()` (sheet.ts:2247-2259), invoked from view/worksheet.ts:5248, which drops the buffer when the snapshotted rows/columns' axis IDs no longer match (sheet.ts:383). The reviewer's cited grep line numbers do not correspond to this repository's file.
